title: Writing 2 · Sunday Writing ✍️
subject: Writing
source_note: Two 20-minute tasks like the 40-minute exam block. Marked by Claude with wiki/English/Writing_Rubric.md after export.

questions.stem:
Write a story in which a character finds something that does NOT belong to them.

What is it? What do they decide to do, and what happens because of that choice?
tips: Start in the middle of the moment they find it, not with 'One day…'.
The heart of the story is the CHOICE: show them hesitate (hands, breath, thoughts).
Use one or two lines of dialogue, with speech marks and a new line for each speaker.
End by showing how the choice changed something, even something small.
checklist: I used at least three precise, interesting words
I varied how my sentences start
I checked spelling and punctuation at the end
My character makes a clear choice, and the ending shows what it led to
questions.technique: Plan, write, check: 3 min / 15 min / 2 min.
questions.source: ACER SEHS Writing block: two tasks in 40 minutes; marked with wiki/English/Writing_Rubric.md

questions.stem:
“Every student in Years 7 and 8 should learn to cook at school.”

Do you agree or disagree? Write a persuasive piece to convince your principal.
tips: Decide your side in the first minute and say it clearly in your opening paragraph.
Give 2–3 reasons, each in its own paragraph, with a real example (a meal, a skill, a cost).
Answer one argument from the other side: 'Some people say… However…'.
You're writing to the principal: be polite and confident, not chatty. End with a strong last line.
checklist: I used at least three precise, interesting words
I varied how my sentences start
I checked spelling and punctuation at the end
I answered one argument from the other side
I wrote for my audience (the principal)
questions.technique: Opinion → reasons with examples → counter-argument → conclusion.
questions.source: ACER SEHS Writing block: two tasks in 40 minutes; marked with wiki/English/Writing_Rubric.md
